bull.b: Consecutive year-over-year growth combined with higher gross margin indicates improving commercial traction and better economics per dollar of revenue. If sustained, this combination can provide greater operating leverage and support investment in the company’s platform transition over the next several quarters.

Deep relationships with leading pharmaceutical companies and a record of programs reaching clinical trials support credibility in a regulated, technically demanding market. This customer access and demonstrated scientific relevance can improve the company’s ability to win platform partnerships and expand existing engagements.

Moving from discrete fee-for-service work toward platform partnerships may increase participation in the economics of assets created with customers. Over time, this model could improve revenue durability, deepen client integration, and create more scalable value across multiple discovery programs and workflows.

bear.b: Persistent operating losses are translating into substantial cash outflows rather than remaining primarily non-cash accounting charges. Continued burn can consume available liquidity, increase reliance on external financing, and restrict the company’s ability to fund ReefIQ, internal pipeline work, and commercial expansion independently.

The sharp reduction in the capital base reflects the cumulative effect of sustained losses and leaves less balance-sheet capacity to absorb execution setbacks. If losses continue, further erosion could weaken financial resilience and make future funding or strategic investment more consequential for existing stakeholders.

The strategic shift toward recurring platform revenue has not yet produced predictable contract timing or revenue visibility. Milestone-based early work and extended customer reviews can delay conversion of the funnel into annual recurring revenue, making near-term scaling dependent on adoption and execution.
